# @ouro.bot/shepherd

Shepherd keeps the GitHub Copilot app's sessions as work. Plain ESM, no build step, no runtime dependencies, Node 22.18 or newer.

## Library

- `import { deps, snapshot, sendTo, archive, exchange, appReady } from '@ouro.bot/shepherd'`
- `deps({ copilotHome })` returns `{ copilotHome, now, sleep, sql, history, historySize, exchange }`. `sql` is a read-only query of `<copilotHome>/data.db`.
- `snapshot(deps, now?, skip?)` returns one object per local, unarchived session: `id`, `title`, `mode`, `state` (`busy` or `idle`), `why`, `running`, `interrupted`, `workspaceId`. Sessions over 500 MB, or idle for over 24 h, are `idle` with a `why`.
- `sendTo(deps, id, prompt, waitMs)` returns `{ ok, reply, error }`. It restores a compressed history first, best effort; a restore that can't run never stops the send.
- `archive(deps, row, { keepWorktree, waitMs, compress })` archives `row.workspaceId` as a workspace, deleting its worktree only when `row.workspaceType === 'worktree'` and `keepWorktree` is not set. Without a workspace it archives the session. Returns `{ ok, session_id, error, compressed }`.
- `compressHistory(deps, id, { dryRun })` gzips an archived (or unlisted) session's `events.jsonl` to `events.jsonl.gz` and returns `{ id, ok, before, after, why }`. It refuses a live session, a file a process has open, and an existing `.gz`. Each compression appends a `history-compressed` row to the disk ledger.
- `restoreHistory(deps, id)` gunzips a compressed history back and returns `{ id, ok, restored, why }`.
- `exchange(copilotHome, messages, { done, keep, waitMs })` and `appReady(deps)` talk to the app's socket on `<copilotHome>/run/ws.port` and `ws.token`.
- `resume(deps, { targets, startedAt, restartedAt, why, lanes, t, log })` sends each target one resume message and waits for a turn; `targets` comes from `pickTargets({ before, after, also })`, `resumeText({ at, why, lanes })` is the message. `RESUME_T` holds the default timings: `grace` (the caller's wait before its snapshot), `delivery`, `retry`, `tries`, `concurrency`, `backoff`. A history over 500 MB is held through `deps.heldBack`, never sent. When anything resumed it writes `<state>/resume-last.json`.
- `loopState(lines)`, `lastTurnAt(lines)`, `continuedSince(lines, since)`, `tookTurnSince(lines, since)`, `lastReply(lines, since)`, `readTail(file, bytes?, { keepPartial? })`, and the `READY` and `DEFER` tokens read a session's history.
- `rows(deps)` returns the sidebar's sessions over the app's socket: `id`, `name`, `state` (`working`, `waiting`, `stuck` or `idle`), `detail`, `isRunning`, `remote`, `coordinatingCreatorSessionId`, `parentSessionId`, `workspaceId`, `workspaceType`, `branch`, `projectRepo`, `openPullRequest`, `automation`, `awaiting`, `lastActivity`. Throws `ShepherdError` when the app is not serving.
- `retireSessions(rows, deps, { apply })` archives handed-off sessions (their successor took a turn, and they were idle five minutes) and finished orphans (coordinator gone, a day idle). `noticeOversizedSessions(rows, deps, { apply })` flags histories over 500 MB, asks for hand-offs, and archives idle giants. `watchRetire(deps, { apply })` runs both, retire first. `apply` false is a plan that changes nothing. Each returns actions `{ what, id, name, reason, done, why }`.
- `retireConfig(file?)` reads `~/.config/shepherd/retire.json` (`SHEPHERD_RETIRE_CONFIG`): `{ "enabled": true }` turns the retire duty on; no file is off.
- `wakesConfig(file?)` reads `~/.config/shepherd/wakes.json` (`SHEPHERD_WAKES_CONFIG`): `{ "enabled": true, "runners": [{ "name", "command": [argv], "everySeconds", "delivery", "session"? }] }`; off unless enabled. `runDueWakes(deps, runners, due)` runs the due runners and delivers each wake (one at a time per session, `replaces` takes back queued messages, `done` reports each delivery). `planWakes(runners)` shows what they would send and sends nothing.
- `stuckResumeConfig(file?)` reads `~/.config/shepherd/stuck-resume.json` (`SHEPHERD_STUCK_RESUME_CONFIG`): `{ "enabled": true }`; off unless enabled. `stuckPlan(rows, deps)` plans; `resumeStuck(rows, deps)` sends one resume to each stopped session, once per stop and at most three a day.
- Errors are `ShepherdError` with `code`, `problem` and `fix`; the message reads `<problem>. Fix: <fix>.`
- `operate.mjs` (exported): `sessions(d, { state })`, `session(d, id)`, `messages(d, id, count)`, `send(d, { session_id, message, delivery_mode })`, `create(d, args)`, `answer(d, args)`, `plan(d, args)`, `archiveSession(d, { session_id, owner_asked })`, `show(d, id)`, `automation(d, args)`, `automationOf(d, id)`, `workflows(d)`, `runWorkflow(d, id)`. Each returns a plain object, or throws `ShepherdError`.
- `listenPrompts(d, { retryMs })` keeps the observer connection that records the questions and plans sessions ask; `applyFrame(pending, frame, at)` applies one announced frame.

## CLI

- `shepherd status [--json] [--copilot-home <dir>]`: one line per local session.
- `shepherd restore-history <id> [--json]`: puts back an archived session's compressed history, for a session unarchived by hand.
- `shepherd watch [--quiet] [--json]`: one pass of the six-hour health watch over the resumed sessions (roster from `<state>/resume-last.json`, state in `<state>/health-watch.json`), then exit. A session that stays broken is reported to the agent with `ouro msg`.
- `shepherd watch --every <seconds> [--quiet]`: stays resident. Each pass runs the health watch, then the quota balancer's applied tick (only when its config says enabled), then the sidebar tidy (at most every `everyMinutes` in `sidebar.json`, only when enabled), then the retire duties (only when `retire.json` says enabled), then the wake runners and the stuck resume (only when `wakes.json` and `stuck-resume.json` say enabled). Passes never overlap; a duty that throws is logged and the next still runs.
- `shepherd watch --status [--json]`: what the health watch is following: healthy, waiting, asked again, broken.
- `shepherd quota [read|plan|status] [--json]`: each Copilot account's quota; plan is what a tick would do; status is the last applied tick. None changes anything.
- `shepherd sidebar [plan|apply] [--json]`: which projects the sidebar shows; plan (the default) changes nothing; apply asks the app to show or hide the changed projects and needs `sidebar.json` to say `"enabled": true`.
- `shepherd retire [plan|apply] [--json]`: retirement and the size watch. plan (the default) changes nothing; apply archives, flags and asks, and refuses unless `retire.json` enables it.
- `shepherd wakes [status|poll] [--json]`: each wake runner's last run, wakes delivered, open wakes and status lines (status, the default). `poll` runs each command now and sends its wakes only when `wakes.json` says enabled; otherwise it prints what it would send.
- `shepherd stuck [plan] [--json]`: the stopped sessions and what a stuck resume would do. plan (the default) changes nothing.
- `shepherd install [--dry-run]`: loads `~/Library/LaunchAgents/bot.ouro.shepherd.plist`, which runs `shepherd watch --every 60 --quiet` and is kept alive. `--dry-run` prints the plist and changes nothing.
- `shepherd sessions [--state busy|idle|waiting|stuck] [--json]`: `{ summary, sessions }` for the sidebar; each session has its activity, coordinator and `awaiting_input`.
- `shepherd session <id> [--json]`: one session, as in `sessions`.
- `shepherd messages <id> [--count n] [--json]`: the last n messages (default 6), oldest first, with `coverage`.
- `shepherd send <id> --message <text> [--delivery immediate|enqueue] [--as-user] [--json]`: `{ ok, status, session_id, name, from, from_session_id, message, error? }`. The message goes as a peer message from Ouroboros' own chat (one durable chat named Ouroboros, kept in the state dir's `identity.json`), shown to the session as a cross-session message, never as the owner's own turn; paths and commands in it are put in inline code so `~` never strikes text through. Replies land in that chat. `--as-user` is only for words the owner asked to be relayed: it sends a user prompt labelled as relayed. `create --prompt` and `plan --feedback` follow the same rule.
- `shepherd create [--project <id|name> | --session-kind chat] [--name] [--workspace-type worktree|branch] [--branch] [--prompt] [--mode] [--model] [--agent] [--reasoning-effort] [--permission-mode] [--json]`: `{ ok, created, session_id, app_url, kind, error? }`.
- `shepherd answer <id> --answer <text> [--json]`: answers a question the resident watch heard the session ask.
- `shepherd plan <id> --approved true|false [--action] [--feedback] [--json]`: approves or rejects a plan the resident watch heard.
- `shepherd archive <id> [--owner-asked] [--json]`: archives a session this agent created, or one the owner asked for with `--owner-asked`, or a handed-off oversize one; the history is compressed in the same pass (restore-history brings it back).
- `shepherd automation <id> [--clear | --interval … --prompt …] [--json]`: reads, replaces or clears the session's automation.
- `shepherd workflows [--json]` and `shepherd run-workflow <id> [--json]`: list the app's workflows, run one now.
- `shepherd open <id> [--json]`: shows the session in the app's window.
- Each agent verb also takes one JSON object on stdin with `--input -`; `--json` prints one JSON result (`{ ok: false, code, error }` on failure). Exit 0 ok, 1 refused or failed, 2 usage.
- `shepherd version [--json]` (also `--version`) prints the installed version.
- `shepherd help`.
- Run it without installing: `npx github:ourostack/shepherd#v0.7.0 status --json` (not on npm yet).
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 the app's data could not be read, the history could not be restored, the agent could not load, or the app refused a sidebar change, 2 usage. Errors are one line.

## Quota balancing

- `quotaConfig()` reads `~/.config/shepherd/quota.json`; the balancer is off unless it says `"enabled": true`. `quotaTick(deps, { apply })` plans (apply false) or applies a tick; `quotaRead(deps)` reads each account's quota; `quotaStatus()` is the last applied tick; `listenQuota(deps)` keeps the app's quota broadcasts in `~/.config/shepherd/quota-app.json`.
- Files, each overridable by `SHEPHERD_QUOTA_CONFIG`, `SHEPHERD_QUOTA_STATE`, `SHEPHERD_QUOTA_APP`, `SHEPHERD_QUOTA_WAITING`, `SHEPHERD_QUOTA_LOG`: the state, the waiting list (`waiting-on-operator.quota.json`) and the decision log (`~/Library/Logs/shepherd-quota.jsonl`).

## Sidebar tidy

- `sidebarConfig()` reads `~/.config/shepherd/sidebar.json` (`enabled`, `homes`, `everyMinutes`); off unless `"enabled": true`. `SHEPHERD_SIDEBAR_CONFIG` overrides the file.
- A project shows when it is a home (its `main_repo_path` is in `homes`) or holds an unarchived session, local or cloud; otherwise it is hidden. `sidebarPlan(projects, sessions, { homes })` is pure; `sidebarTidy(deps, { homes, apply })` reads the app's database and, with apply, sends `set_project_sidebar_visibility` only for projects that change.

## Rules

- Shepherd is read-only except `sendTo`, `archive`, `compressHistory`, `restoreHistory`, `resume` (its record in the state folder), `watch` (its state folder and the agent notice), the retire duties (their state folder, the archive log, and the agent notice; only when `retire.json` is enabled), the wake runners and the stuck resume (their state folder, and the wakes and resumes they send; only when `wakes.json` or `stuck-resume.json` is enabled), `install` (the launch agent), an applied quota tick (its state, log and waiting files, and the re-pins and messages it decides on, only when its config is enabled) and `sidebarTidy` with apply (the app's show or hide requests, only when `sidebar.json` is enabled). It compresses only archived or unlisted sessions, never a live one. It never quits or relaunches the app; that is Housesitter's job.
- Every failure says what probably happened and the fix.
- Tests run against fakes (`test/fake-app.mjs` is a pretend socket). The real database test and CLI status test run only where `/usr/bin/sqlite3` exists.
- Keep it small. A duty moves here only when a caller needs it.
